title: 1-on-1 With Vega Ioane | Baltimore Ravens
text: Ravens fans, I'm so excited to sit down with the newest member of the team, first-round pick Vanga Yawane. Vanga, congratulations. Welcome to Baltimore. >> Thank you so much. I appreciate it. So, you walk in this building and you are officially a Raven. You have the Ravens hat on right now. What are the emotions as you come to the reality that you are a member of this team? I'm happy. Something that stood out to me in hearing from you after you were picked and from the Ravens is that when you came here for your visit, it sounded like everybody felt like this is a match made in heaven. Take me back to that day. What were your thoughts when you were here and when you left this building? [music] When I left, it was definitely a good feeling. Um for me as I went through the entire building, met a lot of people. Biggest thing that stood out to me was that it was a family. You know, it wasn't a It wasn't a job interview or anything like that. Everybody made me feel comfortable. Uh everybody here was just good people. You know, I had a good time. Just had normal conversation with everybody I met with, so. And and as you go through this draft process, you meet with so many people, so many teams. What was it that made it feel like this is a family atmosphere, a place that I could really see myself? Um the meeting that I had with Jamison to start off. You know, we just sat in there and just talked. You know, that's all it was. You know, I love when people can just have, you know, normal conversations, things like that, so. But knowing that this place is, you know, history. There's a lot of, you know, legends that came through here, a lot of good people that came through here, so. I'm excited for that. Part of the family atmosphere, I'm sure, is the connection that you've already started to build with your offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford. And we got a taste of that last night when he got on the call to welcome you to Baltimore. Yes, sir. What was it like when he got on that phone call last night? Hey, WHAT'S UP, BIG DOG? YEAH, YEAH, what's up, man? I was really excited, man. You know, I was a little, you know, little emotional going through it, but as soon as he got on, he got me hyped, so that's how it was. And what has the process been like getting to know him? It's been real cool. Uh he was at my pro day. You know, he held the bag for me as I went and I was showing, you know, putting him on a little bit. That's how it was, but he's a good guy. You uh will have a chance to block for Lamar Jackson, one of the best, if not the very best player in the NFL. What are your thoughts about the responsibility and the opportunity that that presents? Yeah, for me, when I get here, the biggest thing is, you know, earning the right to block for him, you know, and all the other guys. You know, I got to earn my keep, but knowing that I got a quarterback like that, it's going to make my job easier. Now, something that stands out to me, and everyone has said this, is your mentality. And we've got a taste of it uh since since drafting you, just some of the things that you've said and you've talked about. Nobody touches my quarterback. >> Nobody's going to touch my quarterback, man. Simple as that. Nobody's going to stand in front of me and survive. That's my biggest mentality. >> the mentality that you have, the switch that you flip when you get on that field. Where does that come from? >> Yeah, playing the game of football as an O-lineman, you're always going to have that mentality, you know. You got to come in thinking that you have to be the best player on the field. You know, you're playing O-line, but you're playing with four other guys that got to be playing as one. You know, with the guy behind you that we got to protect, you got to have the mentality of nobody's going to touch him. That's That's it for me. You know, not every offensive lineman has highlights, but you've got some highlights, okay? And I want to share some with you here. I want you to run through a couple of these plays here because I think this speaks to the mentality that we're talking about here. So, I got two plays here and you can start it. Take me through this play, and you know this one probably right off the bat. >> Yes, sir. Yeah, man, uh our OC, you know, put a lot of trust in me, you know, coming in motion playing H on the slot, you know, but biggest thing for me is going into the week knowing exactly what I was supposed to do. >> [music] >> Coming down, I'm just trying to kill somebody. Knowing it's a it's a free shot to, you know, just hurt somebody, play physical football, and that's exactly what it was. >> When you get out in space like that, I mean, that's an opportunity that Is that an offensive lineman's dream when you're moving full steam ahead like that? Absolutely. It's something you want to do as a as an O-lineman. >> I mean, you know, you could add a little, you know, fake, get out there on the flat, get the ball, but, you know, we'll see how that works out. And then the other one here is uh here we go. The same play, line up outside, but instead of, you know, killing the D-end, just faking him out and then getting out in space and blocking that corner for the quarterback. You know, didn't work out, but, you know, just having that trust in me to get out there and block a fast corner, that's that means a lot to me. I don't see offensive linemen putting fakes too often on tape, but you did it on that play. Is that Talk me Tell me about that a little bit. Biggest thing is you got to be athletic and have trust in yourself to do something like that. You know, you're running full speed and in a tight space, you got to be able to, you know, take a little jab step and then get out, so. And then one other thing I want to ask you about is, you know, there's this mentality, this tenacity that we're talking about, but there's also this humility. There was the clip as as you've seen many times of you helping the equipment guy push the cart up up the ramp. Talk to me about this humility side, you know, not the mentality, the nastiness that you play with on the field, but that aspect of things as well. I mean, it's as simple as how I grew up. You know, my parents uh you know, taught me a lot of things, but that video, you know, going around, whatever, is cool, but it was nothing more than just helping out somebody who needed help. You know, it's nothing more than that, so. And lastly, when you get on the field this year for the Ravens, what do you want to do? What do you want to accomplish? For me, when I come in, you know, I understand how the game of football works. Nobody wants to hear from a rookie. They want to see, you know, what they can do, how they can earn their keep, things like that, so. That's my entire mentality coming in. Awesome. Well, we can't wait to see you on that field. See you get to work. Appreciate it. >> Appreciate y'all.

title: Exclusive 1-on-1 With TJ Parker! | Buffalo Bills
text: The Buffalo Bills select linebacker TJ Parker from Clemson. >> TJ Parker, welcome to Buffalo. The Bills select you with the 35th overall pick. When Buffalo called your name last night, you told head coach Joe Brady, "I'm ready to hunt." How will you hunt in your rookie season? >> Man, that's just me being and doing whatever I can. Um, you know, we have a great veteran group. Uh, guys like Bradley Chub and Oliver, Greg Russo. I'm gonna get to those guys and try to learn from them as much as possible and and and compete. You know what I'm saying? Come in, be a great teammate, and like I said, hunt whatever it takes to do to win, whether that's special teams, you know, get on the field, do whatever it takes, hunt. I'm I'm a dog, so I got I got to eat. So, whatever that takes, just having that mentality, man, I can't wait and I'm excited. So, >> what's one draft night memory that you won't ever forget? Um, just seeing my parents' excitement, you know, when I first got the call, my heart was racing to the point where you can feel my heartbeat on my arms and I was, as soon as I got the call, I was stunned. I mean, I didn't really know to say it. Kind of was just shocked and just just trying to be in the moment. And to see my parents just jump for joy and just be excited that I'm going to Buffalo. Um, it really meant the world to me. >> Speed to power is your game. You have violent hands that wear out an opposing offense. You said, "I want to put the pain on somebody." Where will your skill set show up most in Buffalo? >> Uh definitely in the run, you know, and in the pass game as well, but um for me, I'm a physical player who who doesn't shy away from contact. You know, I try to put my body on on somebody else on the offense every play I get, you know what I'm saying? And over time, that wears them down like you said. U you know, I want my opponent to to lead the game knowing that that TJ Parker was on their head all night. Um and regardless of what they got to do, um you know, for me, that's just how I love playing the game. Very physical and violent. contact and being physical. It It hurts. You have to be willing to do it. Where did you learn that I'm okay with this pain and I want to inflict it on you? >> Since four years old, you know, me and my brother used to rough house all the time. I love WWE as a kid. So, just trying those moves out. You get to you build the callus up of of getting bumps and bruises. When I told my mom I want to play football at four years old, I said I want to hit somebody and she threw me right into football. And I loved it. I get to fly around, hit people as hard as I can, and there's no consequence to it. So from there, I just knew I love the game. So that's where that comes from. >> Asking to play football at four years old, do you have an obvious love and passion for the game? Where does that show up on the field most? >> Uh, every play. Um, for me, I love it. Um, it's my it's my safe space where, you know, anything you dealing with, you can go football and know he'll be right there with you. Um, at 4 years old, I loved watching JJ Watt play. You know what I'm saying? as a kid, you know, you grew up in Texas playing little league football, you know, all everybody talks about a Texans. Um, and just seeing how he played the game was just so violent and it was just unbelievable. So, for me, it was just like it was a passion. >> Your pass rush moves are unique. You love to grab hands and rip. You don't see a lot of other pass rushers as effective as you are doing something like that. Where did you pick up some of those moves? >> Um, for me, it came from my high school coach, Adrien Laos. Um, man, I met him in in the seventh grade and we've been working and training just to really understand how to pass rush and how to play defensive end in general. Um, and it kind of just helped me correlate my game um and understand what I need to do and just over time like you said just different pass grabbing wrist and hands and things like that. I think it just came natural just something I I did but didn't really try to do and then over time I just started working it and working it. Um, and it became a skill that I learned um and it became very effective for me. >> General manager Brandon Bean called you a three-own player. you played in 39 straight games, a very durable player. What type of routine did you have to be so durable throughout the season? >> Um, for me it's just it's about, you know, um, taking care of your body. That's the biggest thing. Prehab and then post-workout or postgame or whatever. Um, and I early on, you know, I kind of understood what I needed to do. Um, but Clemson does a great job of bringing back their their league guys and their vets and they come and train there. um really seeing how they treat their body, how they come in hours before the workout, taking care of their body, stretching, warming up, hot tub, cold tub, whatever they do. And even afterwards, um it really opened my eyes like, man, I'm trying to get to, you know, where they're at. Cuz you got guys like Christian Wilkins, Dexter, you know, um making hundreds of millions of dollars. Um whereas and I'm trying to get there at one point. So if they're doing it, I should be doing it as well. Um and then over time as I'm growing, I see what works for me and I kind of implement it that way. Um and really, you know, just building that great schedule as I got older, it really helped me. uh you know play a lot longer and then recover a lot faster. So >> 41 and a half tackles for loss in 39 games. You get after it when you're in the game in terms of getting after the quarterback. What are you thinking every rep, >> man? It's like you don't even know how to explain it. You just know when when it's time to rush the passer, it's like it's like a dog staring at a toy. You know what I'm saying? You know exactly what you want and you can't you got to have it. Um for me, it's like my eyes get real big and I know what time it is. It's like a different mode when you know you get to rush the passer um and get a sack because after you make the play, you know, you hear the crowd cheering, you see teammates celebrating with you and like that's the moment you try to chase. So, >> you come from a military family. Your dad was in the army. How does that lifestyle set you up for the NFL? >> Um for me, you know, just creating great balance and structure. You know, my dad was always uh somebody, you know, who who had a great structure around him, great people around him, and you know, he taught me a lot of values when it comes to how I treat people and how to represent yourself. My dad always told me the greatest thing I'm going to give you is your last name. Don't do nothing to ruin it. Um, so at an early age, I knew to treat everybody with respect and to go about my way in a mature manner. Um, and it really helped me, you know, make a lot of great decisions in my life. Um, and then, you know, translate to football field. >> Did you do any crazy military workouts growing up? any any like five minute wall sits or anything like that that we can expect from you? >> We had a we had a couple of them wall sits uh for sure. I ain't going to get into too much detail, but just know like you know we we was well we was good kids you know uh my dad you know he ain't pushed the workouts on us too early but as I started getting older we did a lot of a lot of tire pushes, a lot of flips and stuff like that in the yard. A lot of carries. Um so it was definitely helpful for my football career. What are three words that best describe TJ Parker's personality? >> Uh, funny. Um, um, spontaneous, uh, and loving. >> What's one thing that most people don't know about you? >> I know HOW TO SEW. >> OH, >> YEAH. My mom was a seamress and she modeled for 20 years. So, she taught me how to sew. So, like if I had to fix up jeans or I can make my own hoodie. It's crazy. Um, when I was committing to Clemson, I took Tapestry blankets out of Clemson material and I made my own hoodie. Um, and I wore it when Coach Swinny came and ate breakfast and stuff with us. I still have it. Um, it's in my closet somewhere. Um, but yeah, I know to sew. >> Okay, we're going to have a TJ Parker brand later on in life where where you're sewing in your free time, releasing merch for Bills fans. >> Hey, eventually eventually once I get settled in, we can make something like that work. >> Let's go rapid fire here. What's your favorite hobby? >> The golf. >> What are you best at? My favorite club is a seven iron, but other than that, you know what I'm saying? I can hit the ball consistently. That's it. I ain't saying I'm good. I ain't saying to go straight, >> but I can hit the ball. That's all that matters. It's peaceful. >> Consistently is really good in the game of golf. Some people really struggle with consistency. >> Yeah. And it it teaches you how to be calm because you can't be mad at nobody but yourself. So, >> what's on the pregame playlist? >> Oh, NBA Young Boy. >> What's on your pregame routine? Do you do anything crazy? Um, I drink a Red Bull right before the game and I hate the smelling salts. They get me going. >> Red Bull and smelling salts. >> Yeah. >> Describes the dog that you are, how you get into the game and how you want to hunt. >> Yeah, for sure. It It act It activates me right before I go out and I just turn into a different person. So, >> are you slamming the Red Bull or are you drinking it over over some time? >> Oh, no. I'm chugging it. I'm chugging. >> We're chugging it. Yeah. What's your favorite food? >> Uh, chicken. >> Chicken. How do you like it cooked? >> Uh, I like it roasted. oven roasted. >> And finally, what's one thing you want to tell Bill's Mafia? You can look into the camera right there. >> Bill's Mafia, you guys are getting a dog. Somebody I'm going to do whatever it takes to win so you guys can be satisfied and I'm in the fight with y'all and I love y'all. >> TJ Parker, welcome to Buffalo. That blue looks good on you, man. We're happy to have you here. >> I'm happy to be here and I can't wait to get going.
